naPolicy.dimension4: Constraint Explicitness — N/A for every unit. Budget/timeline/team/compliance/performance axes are owned by meta/constraints.md, which is outside this domain's unit set. Units reference it (e.g. domain Q-06 cites the locked Cloudflare Workers constraint) rather than restating it.
naPolicy.dimension5: Success Measurability — N/A for every unit. Success metrics/KPIs are an ideation-index/meta artifact; no unit in this domain carries a metrics section. Behavioural thresholds inside the units (14d stale, 45d abandonment auto-close, 3 business-day auto-accept floor, 500-char free-text cap) are scored under Problem Clarity / Feature Completeness, not here.
naPolicy.dimension6: Competitive Positioning — applicable to the domain unit only (its Overview names SoundBetter/AirGigs/Fiverr Pro plus a specific capability gap and a moat). N/A for the seven sub-domain units, which are internal decompositions and were never in scope to position.

units.notes: 18 cross-cuts, 4 domain principles, 12 open questions all with owner + deferral target, 6 rejected pairs. Children table matches the folder tree exactly (7 sub-domain dirs, 32 leaf files verified on disk). D3 downgraded for the CX-12 capacity/issuance contradiction; D7 downgraded for one bare [PENDING] with no owner and no deferral target.

9 files, 7 leaves, deepest unit in the domain (05.01.01/02/03 are [DEEP] with 9/14/13 DT annotations). Every open question carries owner + target; every [PENDING] marker carries either a deferral target or a Q-reference. D3 downgraded for one blocking contradiction (craft mutability) plus five warnings.

05.02.01 is the strongest single file in the domain — 20 decisions, a normative Carried Terms table, a closed set of offer-voiding events, and an explicit two-senses-of-acceptance disambiguation (DT-13). D3 downgraded solely for D-15's benchmark-band conflict with 05.01.

8 files. The two bare [PENDING] precedence markers in 05.03-engagement-lifecycle-cx.md (CX-03 §5, CX-04 §5) are stale rather than malformed — both are resolved downstream (05.03.05 D-16 'delivery wins'; 05.03.03 D-10 'revision beats auto-accept'), so D7 is not downgraded. D3 downgraded for two blocking contradictions plus three warnings.

Cleanest unit in the domain. 05.04.01 specifies the auto-accept window's floor (3 business days), ceiling (30 calendar days), escalation ladder (delivery / 50% / T-24h / T-1h), retry policy (2s/8s/32s), a 120-second revision grace, and pauses the clock when notification channels hard-bounce. Only defect found is the QC-override wording.

All four leaves resolve to one invariant ('the credit follows the hands'), reached independently four times and recorded once at domain level as P-02. Every bare [PENDING] in 05.05.03 maps to a Q in the same file (Mandate Lapsed → Q-02; studio assignee → Q-04). 05.05.04 is proposed `wont` for MoSCoW (index D-03), which fairly bounds its expected depth.

Carries the domain thesis. 05.06.01 elects per copyright with required parameters per posture and a closed vocabulary; 05.06.03 specifies which legs are inside the atomic commit and which are outside, and distinguishes Voided from Superseded. D3 downgraded for the unmapped `spec` pricing model; D7 for one bare untracked [PENDING].

All five files [SURFACE]; sub-domain resolved to COULD priority (index Q-03). The deliberate non-relationship with the 05.03 lifecycle is documented at both levels (index D-02, domain CX-08), which is the right call for a shared entity with a different state machine. D3/D7 each downgraded once.

findings.claim: Whether a seller may change the craft of a live listing is specified both ways: 05.01.01 blocks it as immutable, 05.01.02 permits it. Neither statement carries a marker or references the other.
findings.evidence: 05.01.01-service-listings-packages-rate-cards.md:191 — "| D-10 | Craft is immutable on a live listing — archive and republish | Craft determines the legal model set, facet set, benchmark cohort and reputation cohort. A mutable craft is reputation laundering via a form field. |"; 05.01.01:82 — "| Seller changes the **craft** of a live listing (Mixing → Mastering) | Blocked. ... | \"You can't change the craft of a live listing. Archive it and publish a new one — your Mixing reviews stay with Mixing.\" |"; contradicted by 05.01.02-service-category-taxonomy-attributes.md:105 — "| **Seller edits craft on a listing with accumulated reputation** | Reputation is **per-role** (Reviews cross-cut; `05.01.01` DT-03) — changing craft does not carry mix reviews onto a mastering listing. **The edit is permitted; the reputation does not follow** | \"Reviews stay with the work you did. This listing starts fresh in Mastering.\" |" and by 05.01.02:95 — "| **Listing's craft changes while a quote derived from it is live** | Listing version increments; the issued quote honours its own snapshot until expiry |"
findings.forcedInvention: Which of the two mutually exclusive rules governs the craft field on a published listing, and therefore whether the archive-and-republish path is the only route. Both files supply finished user-facing copy for their own outcome, using the same Mixing→Mastering example.
findings.note: 05.01.02's own D-12/D-13 cover curation-driven craft *remap*, which is a different actor; line 105 is explicitly the seller editing.

findings.claim: A below-scale union render is specified as auto-raised to the floor and as blocked, in the same file, for the same trigger — including inside a single table cell.
findings.evidence: 05.01.03-music-pricing-model-library.md:76 (Happy Path 9) — "the rendered fee is floored at scale for that session type; a below-scale render is raised to the floor with the reason shown, **or issue is blocked**."; :103 — "| Union scale floor applies (05.02.03) | Rendered fee is floored at scale; a below-scale render is blocked |"; :104 — "| Union scale exceeds the seller's own rate | The floor wins. ... | \"Your rate is £400; AFM scale for a master session is £480. Priced at £480.\" |"; States table :131 — "| Floored | Union scale exceeds the rendered fee | Price raised to scale ... |" and :132 — "| Blocked | Below a statutory or union floor ... |"
findings.forcedInvention: Whether an under-scale rate is silently uplifted or refused. Reconcilable as render→auto-floor and manual-issue→block (05.02.01:102 and 05.02.03 both say issue is blocked), which is why this is a warning rather than blocking — but line 103 asserts both outcomes for one event.

findings.claim: The universal publish-gate parameters are stated to apply to every pricing model regardless of shape, which makes a points-only or spec listing unpublishable, contradicting the feature's own thesis that those shapes exist.
findings.evidence: 05.01.03-music-pricing-model-library.md:49 — "Every model — **regardless of shape** — declares these before it can be published. A model missing any of them is **not publishable**; the listing cannot go live (D-03, D-04, D-05)", where the four are Minimum, Currency, Tax treatment and Rounding rule; :42 defines Points as "**No — zero cash; a rights term**" and :43 defines Spec as rendering "from nothing". D-04 (:186) narrows to "Every **cash** model declares currency and tax treatment" but D-03 (:185) does not: "Every model declares a **minimum**; a model without one is not publishable".
findings.forcedInvention: Whether non-cash models are exempt from Minimum/Currency/Tax/Rounding at publish, or must supply meaningless values. Taken literally, no points-only production listing can ever publish.

findings.evidence: 05.01.04-rate-benchmarking-price-transparency.md:18 — "Sees the same band as a buyer when evaluating a quote."; :37 (Happy Path 5) — "Buyer viewing a quote sees the same band, so the number is contextualised rather than negotiated blind". findings.claim: Percentage add-on composition is untestable as written: they are declared to apply to the subtotal yet also to apply 'in declared order', which are different arithmetic for two or more percentage add-ons.
findings.evidence: 05.01.01-service-listings-packages-rate-cards.md:33 — "A quote is an **ordered evaluation, not a sum** (D-03). Add-ons occur in the real market in three shapes and **they do not commute**"; :38 — "4. **Percentage add-ons** — applied to the subtotal in declared order (rush +50% per 05.01.06; Atmos ×1.5)."; the permitted add-on model set is "{flat, same-unit-as-tier, percentage-of-subtotal}" (:43).
findings.forcedInvention: For rush +50% plus Atmos ×1.5 on a £1,000 subtotal, whether the fee total is £2,000 (each percentage taken on the frozen subtotal, order irrelevant) or £2,250 (compounded in declared order). Nothing in 05.01.03 or 05.02.01 resolves it, and the difference is the take-rate base.

findings.claim: At Capacity is specified only as disabling the Order CTA; whether an at-capacity seller may still receive a quote request and issue a quote is unstated in both the capacity feature and the listing state machine, while the domain CX asserts the ceiling gates quote issuance.
findings.evidence: 05.01.07-seller-capacity-queue-intake-limits.md:64 — "| At Capacity | Ceiling reached | Listings visible, order disabled, next-available date, waitlist CTA |" (no mention of Request Quote); D-03 (:94) — "At-capacity listings stay visible and non-orderable"; 05.01.01:117 — "| Published — At Capacity | Ceiling hit for this craft (05.01.07) | Live listing, Order disabled, waitlist CTA, next-available date |" versus 05.01.01:116 which does spell out the other case ("'Request Quote' only, Order disabled"). services-marketplace-cx.md:137 asserts the opposite obligation: "issuance of a *new* quote is what the ceiling blocks. Failure surfaces at issuance (\"you're at capacity\")".
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the Request Quote CTA and the seller's issue control are present in the At Capacity state.

findings.claim: An 'Action needed' listing state is defined in 05.01.02 and made load-bearing by its 30-day pause countdown, but is absent from the listing lifecycle state machine that 05.01.01 owns, and the two files describe its orderability differently.
findings.evidence: 05.01.02-service-category-taxonomy-attributes.md:118 — "| **Action needed** (listing) | Craft retired/merged; target does not permit this listing's model or a required facet | Listing live under the old label; named missing item; countdown to the day-30 pause |", and :93 — "Affected listings **stay live** under the old label, enter `Action needed`, seller notified at day 0 / 7 / 28; at **day 30** the listing **pauses**". The owning lifecycle table (05.01.01:109-122) lists Draft, Blocked, Published—Orderable, Published—Not Orderable, Published—At Capacity, Published—Stale, Dormant, Paused, Suspended, Archived — and no Action needed. 05.01.03:116 describes the same situation as "new orders are gated pending remap".
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the state exists in the listing machine at all, and whether a listing inside the 30-day window can still take orders ('stay live' vs 'new orders are gated').

findings.claim: The domain CX file resolves the capacity-vs-immutable-offer collision by making the concurrency ceiling block quote issuance; both owning features specify that it does not — it binds ordering only, and issuance merely surfaces an advisory exposure figure.
findings.evidence: services-marketplace-cx.md:136-137 (CX-12 synthesis) — "The count is advisory at the acceptance boundary — it gates *issuance*, never acceptance of an already-issued offer." / "issuance of a *new* quote is what the ceiling blocks. Failure surfaces at issuance (\"you're at capacity\"), never at the buyer's acceptance." Against 05.02.01-custom-quotes-proposals-scope.md:112 — "The ceiling binds *ordering* (05.01.07 D-03), not acceptance."; 05.02.01:68 lists "Seller reaching their capacity ceiling (DT-04)" under **Does not end the offer**; 05.02.01:77 makes the seller's over-ceiling position informational only — "their **outstanding-offer exposure** (\"3 live quotes totalling 14 days of work against a ceiling of 4 concurrent\")"; and 05.01.07 D-03 (:94) gates only orderability. CX-12 also contradicts itself at :139 — "The seller is warned at issuance when near capacity".
findings.forcedInvention: Whether an at-capacity seller is hard-blocked from issuing a quote or merely warned. The two readings produce different products for the seller who is oversubscribed, and 05.02.01's exposure display is only coherent under the second.

findings.claim: Whether a credit is emitted at milestone acceptance is decided in both directions across sibling features, and each cites the other as its authority. Under one reading a cancelled staged engagement emits duplicate credits.
findings.evidence: 05.03.02-milestones-staged-deliverables.md:107 — "| D-06 | Milestone acceptance is a **two-leg commit**: it releases the tranche **and** emits a credit for the accepted stage. |" (also :36 Happy Path 4 and :73 States row). Against 05.03.05-cancellation-abandonment-kill-fee.md:274 — "| D-06 | ... A cancelled engagement **emits** credits for accepted milestones ... | The surface pass said credits are \"not withdrawn\", which reached for the right outcome through a mechanism that does not exist: **no credit is emitted at a milestone at all** (05.06.03 D-01 fires emission at final acceptance). |", and :302 — "**Superseded** — DT-11. **Credits were never emitted at milestones at all.** A cancelled engagement now emits them, privately by default". 05.06.03-rights-transfer-split-execution.md:59 sides with 05.03.02 while citing the decision that denies it — "| **Milestone acceptance** (05.03.02) | Tranche release | **Does not execute** ... | **Emits** — a credit is a fact about work that happened (05.03.05 D-06) |" (repeated :131, and :130 "Credits already earned on accepted milestones stand").
findings.forcedInvention: When credit records enter domain 02 for staged work — at each milestone acceptance, or only at final acceptance/cancellation. Building both as written double-emits every accepted stage of a cancelled engagement into the platform's core asset.

findings.claim: The engagement state machine's trigger for `Closed` is the recall window expiring, while the same file's happy path and the recall feature both put the engagement in `Closed` with the window still open — and the state is defined as read-only, which makes recalls impossible.
findings.evidence: 05.03.01-order-lifecycle-requirements-gating.md:157 — "| Closed | Support/recall window expired (05.03.06) | Read-only; evidence retained. |" Against 05.03.01:101 (Happy Path 10) — "Engagement enters `Closed`, with the support/recall window **still open** (05.03.06)."; 05.03.06-post-delivery-support-recall.md:25 — "A support window opens **at acceptance** and runs for a declared period", :87 D-01 — "A recall is a **post-terminal** state — the engagement stays closed, rights stay transferred, escrow stays released", :62 — "| Window Expired | Period elapsed | Engagement fully closed; read-only |"; and 05.03-engagement-lifecycle-index.md:50 D-02 — "a recall must reopen a *closed* engagement without unwinding its rights transfer".
findings.forcedInvention: Which state an accepted engagement occupies during the recall window, and whether that state permits the artifact replacement a recall requires. Both readings break something: the states table makes Closed read-only during the window, the recall feature requires work inside it.

findings.claim: Two [DEEP] files specify different, incompatible nudge schedules for the same requirements-gate stall, and the second calls its day-7 notice the 'first nudge'.
findings.evidence: 05.03.01-order-lifecycle-requirements-gating.md:107 — "Buyer nudged at **T+24h, T+72h, T+7d, T+14d**; then 05.03.05's escalating abandonment notice" (repeated verbatim in its Consumes list: "gate nudges (T+24h/72h/7d/14d)"). Against 05.03.05-cancellation-abandonment-kill-fee.md:121-124 — "| 7 | **First nudge** — informational | Buyer only |", "| 14 | Second nudge | **Both.** |", "| 30 | **Abandonment Notice** |", "| 45 | **Auto-Close.** |", and D-04 (:272) "Buyer: 7/14/30 notices, close at 45".

findings.claim: The domain CX assigns the retainer feature a pinned-rate flag that protects a contracted rate from rate-card mutation; 05.03.04 contains no such flag, no pinning rule, and no reference to the listing feature at all.
findings.evidence: services-marketplace-cx.md:24 (CX-13) — "**A contracted retainer rate is PINNED against rate-card bulk mutation.**" and :151 — "the retainer (05.03.04) owns a pinned copy. On a bulk mutation, the pinned copy wins — **the retainer exposes a pinned-rate flag** and the card's blast radius must exclude any listing under an active retainer." A search of 05.03.04-retainers-recurring-engagements.md for "pin" returns zero matches; its Behavior, Decisions (D-01..D-04), edge cases and Cross-Cut Notes never mention rate pinning or 05.01.01. The obligation is only visible from the other side (05.01.01:71 edge case and its rate-card field list "pinned-by-contract flag").
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer building 05.03.04 from its own file ships no pinned-rate flag, so the rate card has nothing to exclude and a bulk edit reprices a contracted client — the exact harm CX-13 exists to prevent.

findings.claim: The notes-window duration is given as a flat 48h (24h on rush) in a decision and as a per-craft value as low as 24h in the seed table, with no rule for how rush interacts with a craft whose seed is already 24h.
findings.evidence: 05.03.03-revisions-limits-change-orders.md:220 — "| D-08 | **The notes window** (48h; 24h on rush) bounds note-dripping |". Against the per-craft seed table at :67-79, which sets the notes window to 24h for Mastering — single, Session performance — remote overdub, Vocal tuning / editing, and Audio restoration, and 48h for mixing/production/composition; plus :81 — "**Rush inheritance**: if a rush tier is bought (05.01.06), the **revision turnaround inherits the rush tier**".
findings.forcedInvention: The notes window for a rush mastering single: 24h (craft seed), 12h (rush halving), or 24h (D-08's rush figure). D-15 makes the table the seed source, which is why this is a warning rather than blocking.

findings.claim: The absolute rule that a QC-failing file never reaches the buyer and never starts their clock is stated without exception in two places, and contradicted by the seller-override path specified in the owning QC feature and acknowledged in the same file's happy path.
findings.evidence: 05.04.01-delivery-acceptance-auto-accept.md:210 — "| D-01 | A file that fails QC is not a delivery | It never reaches the buyer and never starts their clock. |"; :152 — "| **QC Failed** | Delivery fails spec | Seller only ... **The buyer never sees a broken delivery and their clock never starts** (05.04 D-02) |"; 05.04-delivery-qc-acceptance-index.md:46 D-02 — "A technically broken file **must never** reach the buyer and start their auto-accept clock." Against 05.04.02-deliverable-spec-automated-audio-qc.md:106 — "| D-04 | A seller may override with a recorded reason, **visible to the buyer** |", its Overridden state (:76) — "Buyer sees the override and the reason at delivery", and 05.04.01:96 (Happy Path 2) — "it passes (**or the seller overrides with a recorded reason, which the buyer will see**)".
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a spec-failing delivery can be published at all. The override is specified with UI and audit consequences, so the intended answer is discernible — but the rule that forbids it is stated absolutely in the feature that owns the delivery gate and in the sub-domain decision log.

findings.claim: Mid-chain cancellation settlement across a bundle's sellers, and the terminal 'Broken' state for a seller exiting mid-chain, are both left [PENDING] with no owner and no open question covering them.
findings.evidence: 05.05.04-multi-seller-bundles-curated-packages.md:55 — "| Cancellation mid-chain | Per-stage settlement across four parties, plus the partial-work problem (05.03.05 DT-03) ×4 | `[PENDING]` |"; :67 — "| Broken | A seller exits mid-chain | `[PENDING]` |". The file's three open questions cover the counterparty (Q-01), cross-seller SLA fault (Q-02) and assembler margin (Q-03) — none covers settlement or the Broken state. 05.03.05's cascade arithmetic stops at Q-06 ("Who pays the kill fees of orphaned sub-engagements"), which is the upstream half.
findings.forcedInvention: How a four-party bundle settles when it dies mid-chain. Materially mitigated by 05.05-multi-party-supply-index.md:47 D-03, which proposes the whole feature as `wont` for MoSCoW.

findings.claim: The `spec` pricing model has no legal rights-posture combination, and its conditional vesting cannot be expressed in the closed posture vocabulary — yet a posture election is mandatory before a listing tier can publish.
findings.evidence: 05.01.03-music-pricing-model-library.md:43 — "| Spec | nothing | **trigger condition** · the term that vests on trigger | speculative writing/production | No — conditional (DT-10) |", and DT-10 rejects mapping it onto points: "spec is **conditional** ... A points deal vests at acceptance". The legal-combinations table in 05.06.01-engagement-rights-posture.md:70-74 has exactly three rows — "Cash-only (flat · per-song · per-minute · day rate · per-stem)", "Points-only", "Fee + points" — none of which is spec. 05.06.01:208 D-07 — "**The posture vocabulary is closed.** Four master postures, four composition postures, no free text, no \"other\", and no rider may qualify what executes", and D-01 — "**No default posture** — an explicit election is required to publish a tier". 05.06.01 Q-07 concedes the adjacent gap ("**Reversion is a common, legitimate term this vocabulary cannot express**") but not this one.
findings.forcedInvention: Which posture a spec listing elects, and how a right that vests only on a future trigger is represented when all four postures execute at acceptance. Publish is blocked without an election, so a spec listing cannot be created without inventing the mapping.

findings.claim: Whether an elected points participation survives a re-recording of the work is marked [PENDING] with no owner, no deferral target and no covering open question.
findings.evidence: 05.06.02-producer-points-backend-participation.md:62 — "| Points on a recording later re-recorded | The 2020s' favourite manoeuvre | `[PENDING]` |". The file's Q-01..Q-04 cover points-only permissibility, authority to grant, where the aggregate check lives, and expected-value disclosure; none covers re-recording. 05.06.03's Q-01..Q-07 do not either.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a re-recording extinguishes the participation the platform registered into 09/10 — a question with a direct royalty consequence and no route to a decision as tracked.

findings.claim: A defect warranty on custodial labour is named as a trade norm with a range instead of a platform behaviour, and nothing decides whether the platform implements one or for how long.
findings.evidence: 05.07.01-repair-tech-luthier-job-flow.md:59 — "| Warranty on the work | Trade norm: **6–12 months** on labour | Different from a mix recall (05.03.06) — this is a defect warranty on physical work |". No decision in 05.07.01 (D-01..D-05), 05.07.03 (D-01..D-05) or the sub-domain index (D-01..D-04) mentions a labour warranty, and none of the eleven open questions across the unit covers it. By contrast the analogous window for creative work is explicitly bounded and owner-tracked (05.03.06 D-03/D-04, Q-04).
